timeline.summary: Field clip and review introduce firmness, attention and the capacity to remain in conversation.
Mikey criticizes permission-seeking and teaches a pressure/relief model using distance, touch, emotion and eye contact; this has serious consent risk.
He frames rushing to collect a contact as escape from interaction and reviews voice level and public expression of intent.
More clips cover personality, routine questions, line-to-online continuity and using friends as reassurance.
Review contrasts strong words with retreating nonverbal behavior, dismisses boyfriend questions as an exit and criticizes script-only teaching.
They discuss sales-like presentation, the value of recording review, and why interaction length or a contact alone does not show mutual investment.
Mikey criticizes over-explaining and closes on practicing consistent expression. The final ASR segment is truncated at media end and is not used as evidence.

visual_findings: All 50 sampled frames were reviewed. They alternate public approaches with two men reviewing footage on a laptop in a hotel room.
Public participants are blurred, but clothing, location, companions and behavior remain potentially identifying.
Frames confirm the same program as mikey-sijiao-006 and show the review method, but cannot establish consent, contact validity or later outcomes.

permissions.reason: Duplicate formal source with a high-risk pressure model, boyfriend-boundary dismissal, public filming and an ASR duration overrun.
